title: Fix review-blocking release and tooling issues
summary: Fixed review-blocking gaps in release package exclusions, runtime artifact hygiene, portable change-control commands, generated summary privacy, change-packet coverage semantics, stale generated release paths, and queue series override atomic writes.
reason: The review found release/data-loss and operator-workflow risks: active config backups and packaging/runtime artifacts could leak into release surfaces, copied change-control commands depended on an implicit Python import path, generated summaries could expose private config backup contents, strict change coverage could not represent directory moves, generated release docs still displayed obsolete change-packet paths, and series override apply could leave partially updated manifests on write failure.
behavior_before: Release/package policy did not exclude all active config backup locations or source-tree runtime artifacts, runtime hygiene still referenced legacy DesktopApp paths, change-control docs/tools exposed non-portable or stale commands, generated summaries could include config backups, strict coverage required every file path rather than allowing intentional directory coverage, generated change docs/manifests displayed obsolete ops/ops change paths, and series apply wrote file overrides row-by-row.
behavior_after: Release/package policy and hygiene checks exclude the active backup/runtime artifact patterns, docs and generator messages use the portable bundled runner, backup sources are excluded from summary generation and orphan-pruned, directory entries cover descendant paths in strict change coverage, generated change outputs normalize legacy change-packet paths for display, and series apply validates all eligible rows in memory before one atomic manifest write.

rollback_plan: Revert this packet's code, docs, test, release policy, generated docs, generated summaries, and manifest changes together. After rollback, rerun the release package policy checks, runtime hygiene checks, targeted Python tests, summary refresh/check, and strict change validation because these fixes intentionally touch release contents, generated operator metadata, and queue manifest write safety.
notes: Risk is high because the fix touches release exclusion policy, generated operator metadata, and queue file-overrides persistence. No FFmpeg/media transcode, subtitle, audio policy, source deletion, pending-publish drain, or WebView filesystem mutation behavior was changed.
